independent_checks.claim: Safe head tags and Q stripping
independent_checks.reason: Every root, Id, Mono, Weak and Lift produces an implication tag, including the zero alias; only Gen produces Q. Thus R/E/falsum are absent and a Q certificate strips to a strictly smaller child.
Root-by-root tags leave only rho1 for Q→F; its equality body cannot match the required quantified body. Weak would require Safe F; Id/Mono/Lift cannot match.

The literal req body makes the only rho1 match equate F with an implication. In clos→N req, rho2 would equate a Q code to F, K would equate the Q antecedent to F, and Weak reduces to forbidden N req. This uses exact req/nks, not an arbitrary Q core.
Weak reduces to forbidden nks. The only flexible rho6 consequent still leaves Q/F children in its antecedent versus R/Q in V; all other roots and closure constructors are excluded by tags.
Weak directly provides Safe a. A rho6 root forces R(a,b)=F and a=b=0, supplied by Id(0). H/K/Id/Lift matches imply a≥R(a,b)>a; Bundle equates R with Q; remaining antecedent tags are disjoint.

Strong induction on size(major)+size(minor) is valid: Mono strips both immediate children; Lift swaps the minor into major position and uses its own child as new minor, decreasing the sum by one. The returned Weak restores at most that one node. Other cases preserve the stated output-size bound; H with rho6 trigger produces Lift(Id(0)) from two one-node inputs.

Translate finite derivations to Safe by constructive MP elimination; absence of R-headed certificates excludes F. Constructor arithmetic and elimination are primitive recursive and the ordinary correctness argument is PA-formalizable.
